name: empty-email-excluded-rejects-everything-invalid
description: An empty-IA5String rfc822Name excluded subtree should reject every leaf with an email SAN under the NSS-lineage convention. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 does not normatively specify what an empty rfc822Name constraint base means.
references: Go name_constraints_test "empty email excluded constraint rejects everything"
Go src/crypto/x509/constraints.go emailConstraints (delegates domain part to dnsConstraints.all)
notes: DER: SEQUENCE { [1] SEQUENCE { SEQUENCE { [1] '' } } } encodes name constraints with one excludedSubtree containing rfc822Name(''). This is injected via unknown_extensions because Python cryptography rejects RFC822Name('').
Go: dnsConstraints.all short-circuits the host-part match; with the excluded set the verdict flips to 'excluded'. Rejects the chain.
GnuTLS: check_email_constraints special-cases an empty excluded rfc822Name with the same 'the CA shouldn't have issued this' logic as check_dns_constraints. Rejects the chain.

OpenSSL: nc_email has no empty-base short-circuit (the 'Empty matches everything' line is only in nc_dns). An empty excluded rfc822Name doesn't match any real mailbox, so OpenSSL accepts the chain - the only validator we test that diverges here.
